report.summary: Chunk 1 of daedalus/eval/mint.py: module docstring, constants, helper functions (_language_family, _is_junk_label, _git, _is_linked_worktree).
risks: _is_linked_worktree | medium | Detection relies on both 'commondir' and 'gitdir' files; if git layout changes, detection may fail. | Verify against git versions and submodule layouts.

handoff.purpose: Define constants, helper functions, and module-level docstring for independent-oracle task minting.

symbols.name: _LANGUAGE_FAMILIES
symbols.note: Dict mapping language names to family names for cross-language filter.

symbols.name: _IDENTIFIER_RE
symbols.note: Regex for plausible identifier shape (unicode-aware, allows $).

symbols.name: _JUNK_KEYWORDS
symbols.note: Frozenset of keywords considered junk labels.

symbols.name: MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD
symbols.note: Integer threshold for confirmations before minted task is usable.

symbols.name: _GIT_TIMEOUT
symbols.note: Timeout in seconds for git subprocess calls.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_MINT_STORE_PATH
symbols.note: Default path for persisted mint store JSON file.

symbols.name: _language_family
symbols.note: Returns family key for a language name; None stays None.

symbols.name: _is_junk_label
symbols.note: Returns True if name is not a plausible identifier or is in _JUNK_KEYWORDS.

symbols.name: _git
symbols.note: Runs git command and returns stdout or None on failure.

symbols.name: _is_linked_worktree
symbols.note: Returns True if repo_root is a git linked worktree.

claims.text: A minted task stores repo as an ABSOLUTE PATH (see _mint_from_diffs) and the mint store is append-only, so that path has to stay resolvable for the whole life of the corpus.
claims.why: Referenced function _mint_from_diffs not present; the claim about path storage is not verifiable here.

claims.text: Detection is the git on-disk contract, not a path heuristic: git worktree add writes .git as a FILE holding a gitdir: pointer, whereas a primary checkout has .git as a DIRECTORY.
claims.why: The code checks dot_git.is_file() to distinguish file vs directory.

claims.text: A bare repo and a plain non-repo directory both read as "not a linked worktree" and are left to the existing git-failure paths
claims.why: If .git does not exist or is not a file, returns False; git-failure paths not shown but the detection returns False.

claims.text: The pointer alone is NOT enough, and this was measured rather than assumed: a SUBMODULE also has .git as a gitdir: file, and a submodule checkout is perfectly permanent -- refusing to mint from one would be a false refusal
claims.why: The code reads the pointer and checks for 'gitdir:' prefix; then proceeds to inspect target structurally, distinguishing from submodules.

claims.text: linked worktree  .git/worktrees/<id>/  HEAD ORIG_HEAD commondir gitdir index logs; submodule .git/modules/<name>/  HEAD config description hooks index info logs objects packed-refs refs
claims.why: The code does not inspect the admin directory contents; it only reads the pointer and checks for 'gitdir:' prefix. The structural inspection is not implemented in this chunk (the function is incomplete).

claims.text: commondir and gitdir together appear only in the linked-worktree admin layout. Requiring BOTH means an unreadable or unexpected target fails toward "not ephemeral", i.e. toward minting
claims.why: The code does not check for commondir or gitdir files; the function is truncated and does not contain that logic.

claims.text: _is_junk_label: True if name cannot be a real symbol label -- see the JUNK FILTER comment above. Checked name-shape-first (a non-identifier like <anonymous> never reaches the keyword set at all). The keyword check is intentionally case-SENSITIVE
claims.why: Function first checks _IDENTIFIER_RE.match(name); if fails returns True. Then checks name in _JUNK_KEYWORDS, which is case-sensitive.

claims.text: _git: Run git in repo_root; stdout on success, None on ANY failure (missing git, not a repo, bad ref, timeout, non-zero exit). Minting must degrade to "nothing minted", never raise
claims.why: Function catches OSError and subprocess.SubprocessError, returns None; also returns None if returncode != 0.

claims.text: _language_family: The cross-language filter's equality key for lang_name -- see _LANGUAGE_FAMILIES above. None (no LanguageSpec) stays None and therefore never equals any real family, same fail-closed behavior as before this grouping existed.
claims.why: Function returns None if lang_name is None; otherwise returns _LANGUAGE_FAMILIES.get(lang_name, lang_name).

observations.what: Function _is_linked_worktree is incomplete; it reads the pointer but does not yet perform structural inspection of the admin directory as described in the docstring.
Docstring claims about 'commondir' and 'gitdir' files are not implemented in the provided code; the function is truncated.
The module docstring makes many claims about behavior in _mint_from_diffs and other functions not present in this chunk; those claims are uncheckable here.
